tonight.headline: Josh Allen's 40.8 is still the only score — and Panda Attack left 22.5 on their bench doing it.
body: Nothing has changed on the scoreboard since this morning, but the Thursday result is now fully priced. Dalton Kincaid caught his way to 22.5 for Panda Attack and did it from slot 20 — their bench — because they moved him out of the tight end slot before kickoff and started Harold Fannin Jr. instead. That is a 22.5-point unforced error on a night your 40.8 counted in full.

ESPN still reads 59%, which remains the honest number rather than a pessimistic one: they have nine unplayed starters and you have eight. Your last man is Isaiah Likely on Monday night, and so is theirs — Davante Adams and kicker Harrison Mevis are both Rams. This does not resolve until Monday. There is nothing for you to do about it tonight.

case.label: Where the 40.8 actually came from
case.body: Allen went 40.8 against Detroit, 17.8 above his 23.0 pregame projection. That is one week of quarterback variance banked against a full slate you have not played, which is why a 40-point lead prices at 59% rather than 90%.

case.label: The script that beats you
case.body: Panda Attack start Dak Prescott, George Pickens and Javonte Williams in the 50.5-total Washington–Dallas game, the highest total on the Week 2 board, plus Saquon Barkley and Chase Brown at 11:00. If Dallas goes over and Barkley gets a 7-point favourite's fourth quarter, they are level before Monday and Davante Adams decides it.

case.label: Their self-inflicted wound
case.body: Fannin Jr. projects 10.1 and Kincaid scored 22.5 from their bench. They also hold Jalen Hurts at 20.2 behind Prescott at 20.2 — a second startable quarterback earning nothing in a one-QB league. This is a manager who is not optimising, which is the single best thing about your 59%.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Davante Adams did not practise Thursday, listed as rest on the Giants–Rams report. If he carries a designation into Monday, their last card weakens and the Likely-versus-Adams Monday duel turns your way. Conversely, if Panda Attack set a correct lineup before 11:00 Sunday, the 59% is optimistic rather than honest.

doFirst.deadlineLabel: Both games kick at 11:00 Sunday Mexico City
doFirst.title: Drop Kyle Pitts, add Rashod Bateman
doFirst.subtitle: Fourth run carrying the Pitts half and I am changing the other half: the incoming name was wrong, and Baltimore's own Friday report named the right one.

case.label: The drop, unchanged and now confirmed
case.body: Atlanta's final Friday report rules Michael Penix Jr. OUT and lists Tua Tagovailoa DOUBTFUL with the oblique. Cooper Rush starts against Carolina. But the quarterback was never the argument: Chem's flex is slot 3, RB/WR only, and Isaiah Likely holds the single tight end slot on an intact thesis. Pitts's 10.4 projection is unreachable in this league — his effective projection is zero. STRATEGY section 9 says it in one line: a second startable tight end has value in IPADE and none here.

case.label: Why the incoming name changed
case.body: For three runs this card said Mack Hollins. Baltimore's Friday report changed the board: Zay Flowers is DOUBTFUL with a hamstring, and BaltimoreRavens.com states plainly that if Flowers sits, 'Rashod Bateman would move into the top receiver spot.' That is a vacated role with a name attached and a club source behind it — STRATEGY section 4's second-strongest add signal.

case.label: Bateman against Hollins on the numbers
case.body: Bateman projects 10.3 this week and 122.7 on the season at 11.3% rostered and rising +1.27 a day. Hollins projects 8.9 and 96.0 at 6.7%. Baltimore carry a 27.75 implied team total against New Orleans, the highest of any team on your board; New England's is 23.25. Bateman is the better player in the better offence with the better number.

case.label: The honest case for Hollins, and why it loses
case.body: Hollins's vacancy is more durable — A.J. Brown is on injured reserve for six games and Bateman's opening needs Flowers to actually sit. But the Yahoo beat writer who names Hollins the favourite then votes DeMario Douglas, because Douglas drew a team-high seven targets while Hollins went 4 for 51 on deep work. In full PPR the deep-target profile is the wrong shape. I take the better offence and the better projection over the longer fuse.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Zay Flowers is active on Sunday's inactive list, which puts Bateman back to third in Baltimore behind Flowers and Mark Andrews and makes this a hold rather than an add. Or Pitts is still on your roster when Atlanta kick off at 11:00 Sunday — in which case this card has failed four times, closes as CHURN, and does not get rewritten a fifth.

whatWentWrong.title: This brief aimed the Pitts card at the wrong receiver for three consecutive runs
whatWentWrong.lead: It named Mack Hollins on Wednesday, defended him Thursday, and re-issued him this morning — while the better free agent was sitting on Baltimore's injury report the whole time.

case.label: What was missed
case.body: The card was built off a FantasyPros waiver column naming Hollins as the A.J. Brown beneficiary. Nobody checked what the Zay Flowers hamstring — which this brief has been tracking since Wednesday in the Mark Andrews row — did to Baltimore's receiver order. Rashod Bateman has been free in Chem at 11% rostered throughout.

case.label: What it would have cost
case.body: Nothing yet, because the card was never executed. That is luck, not process: had you fired it Wednesday you would hold an 8.9-projection receiver in New England's 23.25-point offence instead of a 10.3 in Baltimore's 27.75.

case.label: The process error underneath
case.body: The brief read one waiver column and stopped. STRATEGY section 4 ranks a vacated role with a name attached above an analyst's pick, and the Ravens' own club site supplies exactly that sentence. It was one search away on every one of the three runs.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: If Flowers is active Sunday and Hollins clears six targets in New England's opener without Brown, this correction was itself the error and the card goes back to Hollins on Tuesday.

whatWentWrong.sources: BaltimoreRavens.com · The Big Lead · Yahoo Sports

whatWentWrong.title: Kyle Pitts has now been on your bench for sixty-eight hours with a card telling you to drop him
whatWentWrong.lead: Written Wednesday as DEPTH, raised to SOLID Thursday, carried Friday morning, carried again now. Atlanta kick off in nineteen hours and after that he cannot be dropped at all this week.

case.label: The clock
case.body: Atlanta play Carolina at 11:00 Sunday Mexico City, 17:00 UTC. A player whose game has started cannot be dropped, so the seat freezes until rosters unlock next week if this is not done before then.

case.label: Why it keeps not happening
case.body: I do not know, and I am not going to pretend the card was unclear. What I can do is name the cost honestly: Pitts is the only bench seat on this roster outside the seven-day churn window. Coker arrived 16 September, Likely 13 September. If Pitts's seat freezes, AVIATO has no usable roster move until 22 September.

case.label: The size of the prize
case.body: Small, and saying so is the point. This is a bench seat worth roughly a point a week in expectation, not a season-changer. It is on the list because it is free, not because it is big.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: If Isaiah Likely appears on the Giants' Saturday report — New York play Monday, so they file one — Pitts becomes your only tight end and this card dies on the spot. That is the one scenario in which sixty-eight hours of inaction turns out to have been right.

bench.detail: JAX · at DEN · SUN 14:05 · Trevor Lawrence · Jacksonville's final Friday report records no concerns about the shoulder. Jakobi Meyers is on that report with a thumb and will play. FantasyPros expect Patrick Surtain II to shadow Thomas, which is why the tile is red on a good offence.

He is a genuine flex candidate again and he still loses to McLaurin by half a point and seven points of game total.

worthALook.name: Mark Andrews
worthALook.lead: Still the largest ownership anomaly on either wire, still free here, and the trigger that would make him a card was checked again this afternoon and did not fire.

case.label: The trigger, checked
case.body: The condition on file is 'Isaiah Likely appears on a Giants injury report.' The Giants filed their Friday report for Monday Night Football this afternoon: seven players listed, Likely is not among them, Nabers is not among them. The trigger has now been checked on three consecutive reports and has never fired.

case.label: The merit half got better today
case.body: Zay Flowers is DOUBTFUL and Baltimore carry a 27.75 implied total. Andrews is the second-largest beneficiary of a Flowers absence after Bateman, and the Ravens' passing game is the highest-scoring environment on the board.

case.label: The number that kills it anyway
case.body: Chem's flex is slot 3, RB/WR only. Adding Andrews creates a second tight end who cannot enter any lineup slot — the exact dead seat the Pitts card above is spending a roster move to clear. Adding him while dropping Pitts would be a lateral move into the same trap. Also: New Orleans allowed the twelfth-fewest yards per target to tight ends historically.

case.label: When to act
case.body: The instant Likely appears on the Giants' Saturday report, claim Andrews the same hour and start him Monday in Likely's slot. That is the only path, and New York file a Saturday report because they play Monday.

worthALook.name: Khalil Shakir
worthALook.lead: 69% rostered nationally, sitting on waivers here, and the clearing time is the whole problem: 07:00 UTC on 23 September, after his Week 2 game has been played.

case.label: Why the urgency is fake
case.body: The FantasyPros sleeper note that surfaced him was a Week 2 note. He clears on Wednesday 23 September. By then his Week 2 line is public and the question is a Week 3 one — so there is no version of this where claiming early beats waiting.

case.label: What the claim would cost
case.body: Nothing lasting. Chem priority resets weekly, so a claim is free in the sense that matters. AVIATO sit 10th of 10 this week, so a contested claim loses; next week the order resets and that stops being true.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Six or more targets against Detroit makes him a free claim on Wednesday 23 September, with the drop being whichever of Monangai or Brian Thomas Jr. had the worse Sunday. Fewer than six says the sleeper note was about game script, not role, and the row comes off this list.

worthALook.name: Jakobi Meyers
worthALook.lead: The largest season projection of any receiver on this wire — 182.4 — at 77% rostered nationally and free here. New to this list because Friday's Jacksonville report gave it a reason to move.

case.label: The ownership anomaly
case.body: 77% rostered nationally, free agent in Chem, and 182.4 in season projection, ahead of Worthy at 173.9 and Addison at 171.4. STRATEGY section 4 calls widely-rostered-elsewhere-and-free-here the strongest single wire signal in a shallow league.

case.label: The reason he is a watch and not a card
case.body: Jacksonville's Friday report lists him limited all week with a thumb. He will play, per the same report. A thumb on a receiver is a catch-rate injury and the market has not priced it — his ownership is falling 0.60 a day, not rising. This is a buy, but not before the thumb resolves.

case.label: The structural problem
case.body: You already hold two Jacksonville players in Tuten and Brian Thomas Jr., and STRATEGY flags a week 7 Jacksonville bye problem in both leagues. A third Jaguar deepens a known hole.

case.label: When to act
case.body: If Meyers out-targets Brian Thomas Jr. at Denver on Sunday while Thomas is shadowed by Surtain II, take Meyers for Thomas on Tuesday 22 September when Thomas's seat is the one whose thesis broke. If Thomas wins the target count, this row closes.

doNotChase.name: Jordan Addison
doNotChase.lead: Declined for a fifth consecutive run, and today the quarterback clause that was supposed to rescue him resolved against him for good.

case.label: The condition that failed
case.body: The file said: act if Kyler Murray clears the five-stage protocol and Addison draws seven or more targets. Minnesota ruled Murray OUT on Friday. Carson Wentz starts.

case.label: The number that kills the case
case.body: Sports Illustrated's Wentz fallout piece moves T.J. Hockenson from TE23 to TE14 and leaves Addison unchanged at WR60, with the reason stated flatly: 'Wentz cannot support two viable wide receivers.' Jefferson takes 41% of the receiving yards. Addison is the third read behind a tight end.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Justin Jefferson missing time. Nothing short of that makes the second Minnesota receiver startable while Wentz is throwing, and Murray has no return date.

doNotChase.name: Mack Hollins
doNotChase.lead: This brief told you to add him three times. Today it is telling you not to, and putting him in this section rather than quietly deleting the row.

case.label: What was right about him
case.body: The vacancy is real and durable: A.J. Brown is on injured reserve for six games, Hollins slid into the role the moment Brown left, took 18 of the first 32 snaps and led New England in receiving yards with 4 for 51.

case.label: The number that kills the case
case.body: DeMario Douglas drew a team-high seven targets to Hollins's four. In full PPR a reception is a point before a yard is gained, so the slot receiver with the volume beats the perimeter receiver with the yards. The writer who calls Hollins the favourite by role then votes Douglas by volume, and in this scoring Douglas is right.

case.label: The comparison that settles it
case.body: Rashod Bateman projects 10.3 and 122.7 in a 27.75-point Baltimore offence. Hollins projects 8.9 and 96.0 in a 23.25-point New England offence. Same seat, same cost, better player.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Zay Flowers active Sunday plus six or more Hollins targets against Pittsburgh. That combination reverses this on Tuesday and I will say so.

doNotChase.sources: The Big Lead · Yahoo Sports · BaltimoreRavens.com

doNotChase.name: Romeo Doubs
doNotChase.lead: Carried from yesterday, and today's New England reporting made the fade firmer rather than softer.

case.label: The number that kills the case
case.body: Forty snaps in Week 1 and zero catches. He dropped a potential 25-yard gain and was the target on Drake Maye's first interception. Forty snaps with nothing on them is worse than fifteen snaps with four catches, because it says the offence tried.

case.label: Why he keeps rising anyway
case.body: +0.53 a day. The market is buying the A.J. Brown vacancy and taking the most expensive name attached to it. STRATEGY section 4 is explicit that ownership velocity is a lagging confirmation of role, never a substitute for it.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: New England's Saturday report or beat coverage naming Doubs rather than Douglas or Hollins as the man absorbing Brown's work. Nothing published this week does.

settled.title: Name Mack Hollins as the incoming player on the Pitts card (16–18 September, three runs)
settled.result: Wrong, and corrected today rather than next week. Baltimore's Friday report names Rashod Bateman as the man who moves into the top receiver spot if Zay Flowers sits; Bateman projects 10.3 to Hollins's 8.9 and is free here at 11%. The outgoing half of the card was right all along; the incoming half was one search away for three days.

settled.title: Tell you Michael Penix Jr. was Atlanta's questionable starter (17 September)
settled.result: Wrong, and now fully resolved rather than merely retracted. Atlanta's final Friday report: Penix OUT, Tua Tagovailoa DOUBTFUL with the oblique, Cooper Rush starting against Carolina. The correction stands and the underlying call on Pitts never depended on it.

settled.title: List Romeo Doubs as a SOLID watch-list name (17 September)
settled.result: Wrong, reversed Friday morning, and reconfirmed this afternoon. Forty snaps, zero catches, a drop and an interception. He is in Do-not-chase above and stays there.

settled.title: Claim Jalen Coker and drop Matthew Stafford (14–16 September)
settled.result: Still logged wrong on price and now half-vindicated on the player, which is the honest version. Coker was full Friday, is off the injury report entirely, and went 8 for 138 with two scores on a 24.3% target share in Week 1. The claim was wrong because it cost Stafford, who is about to be free in the other league — not because Coker was a bad player.

settled.title: Hold Isaiah Likely over Kyle Pitts at tight end (14 September)
settled.result: Held, and the trigger checked for a fourth time. Likely is absent from the Giants' Friday report for Monday Night Football; so is Malik Nabers, which is the risk rather than the reassurance. Eight catches on eight targets with two touchdowns in the Giants debut still stands behind it.

settled.title: Start Terry McLaurin in the RB/WR flex (15 September)
settled.result: Held, and now held against a second challenger. Jalen Coker cleared Friday practice and became a live option; McLaurin keeps the slot on 12.5 against 12.0 and on the game environment — 50.5 total at Dallas against 43.5 at Atlanta, where Carolina are 2.5-point favourites and will be running late. He is also absent from Washington's injury report, which closes the quad clause.

settled.title: Hold Justin Jefferson through the Minnesota quarterback change (17 September)
settled.result: Held, and resolved today exactly as the thesis required. Murray is OUT, Wentz starts, and Jefferson is WR6 for Week 2 on a 41% receiving-yard share. The two sources that disagreed on Wednesday no longer disagree.

settled.title: Decline Jordan Addison for the wire (16 September, five runs)
settled.result: Held and now closed on its own condition. Murray did not clear protocol. Addison stays WR60 with Wentz throwing, and the same column that moves Hockenson up eleven places leaves Addison exactly where he was.

settled.title: Hold Brian Thomas Jr. through the shoulder scare (12 September, reviewed six times)
settled.result: Held on availability for the last time this week. Jacksonville's final Friday report records no concerns. The production half is still unproven and he draws Patrick Surtain II on Sunday, which is the real test.

settled.title: Hold Kyle Monangai rather than drop him for a wire back (16 September)
settled.result: Held, and the three-run information blackout ended. Chicago's final Friday practice report has Monangai full with no designation, and D'Andre Swift full as well. The split is unchanged and both are healthy.

settled.title: Hold Tyler Loop at kicker (16 September, five consecutive runs)
settled.result: Held. PFN have Loop K4. The best actually available on this wire is Chase McLaughlin at K6, then Tyler Bass K8 who is on waivers clearing after his game, Eddy Pineiro K12 and questionable, Trey Smack K13, Cairo Santos K14, Evan McPherson K15, Chris Boswell K17. K4 beats all of it and Baltimore's 27.75 implied total is the reason.

settled.title: Hold the Ravens defence rather than churn to San Francisco (16 September)
settled.result: Held, and the underlying case improved. Trey Hendrickson was back at practice Friday after not practising Wednesday. New Orleans carry an 18.75 implied total. The 49ers and Chargers are both still free here and both are Tuesday's question, not today's — the seat is inside the seven-day churn window until 23 September.

settled.title: Decline Mark Andrews on structure (17 September)
settled.result: Held for a third run, with the trigger checked on the Friday report rather than assumed. The merit half strengthened today — Flowers doubtful, Baltimore at 27.75 implied — and the structural objection is unchanged, which is why it is still a decline and not a card.

settled.title: Find no Chem trade worth proposing (17 September)
settled.result: Re-run from scratch on this snapshot rather than carried: every one-for-one pairing between your fourteen players and all 126 players on the other nine rosters, scored on both sides' optimal lineups. Zero produced a gain for both teams, on the week or on the season. Guillo-tinas are the interesting shape — Lamar Jackson starting and Patrick Mahomes on their bench in a one-QB league, with a questionable George Kittle as their only tight end — but you do not need a second quarterback, so there is no deal.

cannotSee.label: Whether Zay Flowers actually plays, which is the whole Bateman card
cannotSee.body: He is DOUBTFUL, he returned to practice Friday, and Baltimore call him day-to-day. Head coach Jesse Minter: 'We will look at and make sure we are putting Zay in the best position.' Doubtful is roughly a 25% play rate historically, but doubtful-and-practising is not the same animal as doubtful-and-absent, and the inactive list does not publish until 90 minutes before kickoff — long after this brief is written.

cannotSee.label: The Giants' Saturday report, which is the Mark Andrews trigger
cannotSee.body: New York play Monday, so their week runs a day later than everyone else's and they file one more report than any other team on your board. Likely is absent from Friday's. If he appears on Saturday's, Andrews should be claimed the same hour and started Monday. Nothing in this brief can see that report.

cannotSee.label: Three of your fourteen tiles are not researched
cannotSee.body: Kyle Pitts, Kyle Monangai and Jalen Coker. I did not retrieve a points-allowed-by-position figure for Carolina's, Minnesota's or Atlanta's defences this run, so those tiles are dashed rather than guessed. Coker's is the one that matters, because it is the tile that would have argued for or against the flex swap — the hold rests on game total and route share instead, and that is a weaker footing than a researched grade.

cannotSee.label: No Houston reporting this run, so Woody Marks came off the watch list unresearched
cannotSee.body: He has been on it for three runs with 'no dated Week 2 Houston usage report retrievable' as the finding. I did not search Houston this afternoon and I am not going to carry a row I did not check. He is a free agent in Chem from 22 September regardless, so nothing is lost by the gap — but the row's absence is an omission, not a judgement.

cannotSee.label: The New England run defence, where two sources flatly disagree
cannotSee.body: FantasyPros' Week 2 primer calls it a 'vulnerable run defence' and projects Jaylen Warren to RB2 on volume. Last Word on Sports, the same day, calls it 'stout'. I have graded Warren AVERAGE rather than picking a side, because the thing I can actually verify — an 18.25 implied team total as a 5-point road underdog — points the same way whichever of them is right.

cannotSee.label: Rivals' pending waiver claims are invisible
cannotSee.body: ESPN only ever returns your own. Mark Andrews at 82% rostered, Jakobi Meyers at 77% and Rashod Bateman at 11% and climbing are the three names most likely to be taken out from under this brief between now and Sunday. Bateman is a free agent, so any rival can take him instantly with no waiver period at all.

cannotSee.label: Season projections are still frozen, so every trade number is suspect
cannotSee.body: seasonProj has produced identical figures across snapshots on four consecutive days for the same players. They do differ correctly between the two leagues, which says the scoring maths is live even if the underlying forecast is not. The Chem no-trade finding above is therefore a finding about August's opinion of these players, not necessarily about today's.

cannotSee.label: Defence grades before week 4 are judgement, not data
cannotSee.body: There is one game of 2026 season data. Every grade on this page rests on an implied team total, a point spread, a named single-game metric or an analyst board — not on a season rank of points allowed to a position, because that rank does not meaningfully exist yet. Treat the tiles as arguments, not measurements.

cannotSee.label: This brief does not refresh
cannotSee.body: It is as old as the snapshot it was built from: 21:52 UTC on Friday 18 September. Nothing in it updates on its own. The next run is Saturday morning, which is after Atlanta's Saturday news but before Sunday's inactive lists — so the Bateman card's central fact will still be unresolved when you next read this.
